description: Establish and document a green baseline for every mandatory local gate before any code change. Confirms the sandbox can run the Android gates locally (SDK installed by planner) so later features are verified against a known-good starting point. No production code changes.
steps: Confirm Android SDK is present at /opt/android-sdk and a gitignored local.properties with 'sdk.dir=/opt/android-sdk' exists at repo root; if missing, recreate local.properties (it is in .gitignore, so it is never committed).
Run the Python boundary gate: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` from repo root and confirm it passes.

Run the Android gates with the pinned Gradle 8.9 binary (/root/.local/share/mise/installs/gradle/8.9.0/gradle-8.9/bin/gradle), JAVA_HOME=/root/.local/share/mise/installs/java/17.0.2, ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk ANDROID_SDK_ROOT=/opt/android-sdk: `:app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug --console=plain` and confirm BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
Attempt (best effort) `:app:assembleRelease` WITHOUT modifying the signing chain; record whether it produced app-release-unsigned.apk.
Record the exact commands and results in the feature findings. Do NOT modify any source file in this feature.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` reports OK (all tests pass).
Gradle 8.9 / JDK 17 `:app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug` reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL against the unmodified base branch.
LAN DEV and Consumer Cloud assembleDebug both report BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
Findings record the exact gate commands and their green results, and note whether assembleRelease is feasible.
